conclusion: Neil Movva (ex-NVIDIA kernels) runs Sal Research as a 'token factory': an API whose job is the cheapest possible tokens, not low-latency Cursor-class chat. He will use every chip, every US power site, and every stack layer; 10× cheaper tokens is a new category. Background vs realtime mix ends 2026 around 50/50 and he wants 90/10 background. Fireworks/Together/Baseten optimized for Cursor latency; he wants throughput. Wafer allocation at TSMC is the gate for Etched-class ASICs. Cerebras-style SRAM/HBM tradeoffs are evaluated, not worshipped.
background: Patrick wants a supply-side tour from transistor to token. Movva's first job was NVIDIA kernels; he hires for love of performance engineering, not years of CUDA. Theme of the company is abundance — treat intelligence as a commodity, not an expensive consultant.
important_facts: Product: Sal Research is a token factory API for open (and customer-sovereign) models. Thesis: whenever something is 10× cheaper it is a new category. He will squeeze more tokens from the same NVIDIA GPU than anyone else, starting at kernels, then every chip/power/land lever in the US. Contrast: Baseten, Fireworks, Together chased low-latency because of Cursor; he thinks that was right a year ago and is now the wrong scarcity.

Workload mix: humans cannot consume 10× more interactive tokens; the slack is background/proactive agents. He forecasts ~50/50 background vs realtime by year-end, then 9010 in favor of background. Long-context (200k) is not the model's core strength if pretrain was 8–16k. Cybersecurity batch (Fable/Mythos-style sweep of every line of code) is the kind of job that wants cheap tokens, not 100ms chat.

Hardware: happy to buy a good fraction of any new chip if TSMC wafers exist — Etched, d-Matrix, etc. fail first on allocation, not ideas. Cerebras: on-die SRAM vs HBM (~10 TB/s on Blackwell-class vs much higher on wafer-scale, different capacity). He will not pretend CUDA years are a hiring filter. Customers increasingly want to own/sovereign the intelligence they depend on.
